transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Drowned Priest [T-04].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The rain has not stopped in eleven years, and tonight it comes sideways off the black water, hammering the plank causeway underfoot. Ahead, torches gutter at a Warden toll-gate — the only dry way into Hollowmoot — where a queue of soaked refugees, eel-sellers, and huddled families wait to be searched, taxed, and counted. Somewhere behind the gate the stilt-town rises on its pilings, lantern-light smeared gold through the downpour, and a watchtower bell hangs silent for now. A Warden sergeant with a ledger and a hooked pole checks hands, throats, and papers for hive-marks before anyone is let through, and the queue is getting nervous.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: That sergeant's not just doing his duty. He's looking for something specific—something he thinks is coming through this line.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps back from the crowd of refugees, keeping to the rain-shadows at the edges of the queue. She watches the sergeant work—his face, the way his hands grip the hooked pole, the precise pattern of his inspections. She notes which people he waves through quickly and which ones he holds up for closer examination of their necks and palms. Beyond the gate, she tracks the torchlight and shadows, counting the wardens waiting inside.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Sergeant, I know what true fear looks like when I see it. You're checking the wrong things—and you know it. Let these people through.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps out from the crowd of waiting refugees, moving deliberately toward the checkpoint. His sharp, weathered eyes—honed from years of reading omens in every ripple and raindrop—fix on the Warden sergeant. He studies the man's trembling grip on the hooked pole, the nervous dart of his eyes, the way he flinches slightly with each new person. The fortune-teller approaches with measured, confident steps, projecting an authority that seems to come from somewhere deeper than mere rank.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Sergeant Doss—I see your hands are full tonight. What troubles these folk more than the endless rain?

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen approaches the toll-gate through the downpour, moving with the authority of someone known here. She notes the sergeant's meticulous work checking for hive-marks, then surveys the nervous refugees—searching their faces and postures for signs of what has them more afraid than usual. She's gathering information before she commits to anything else.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I used to stand where you're standing. I know what you're really looking for.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire approaches the toll-gate with the bearing of someone who once wore a badge, studying the sergeant's technique and the refugees' reactions. She reads his posture, his cadence, the families he lingers on—separating the procedure from the man doing it.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Verrick taught me well—taught me to read fear in a man's face. Let these people through, Sergeant. He and I have unfinished business anyway.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - - 0 -, invoking Served under Captain Verrick [AL-02] → Good (+3) vs Poor (-1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice + - 0 + → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous doesn't just read the sergeant — he *names* what he sees, out loud, close enough that only Doss hears it: fear, real fear, the kind a man carries home and doesn't tell his wife about. The sergeant's hooked pole dips an inch. His jaw works. Whatever Aldous said landed dead center, and now Doss is watching him back instead of the queue. Mire, a half-step behind, clocks the tell for what it is — not diligence, not Order zeal, just a man following someone else's orders past the point where he believes in them anymore. She's seen that exact posture in a mirror once. Between Ysolde's silent count of who gets waved through and Morwen's gentle question landing soft against Doss's guard, the four of them now have the shape of this sergeant laid bare: what he's actually afraid of, and what kind of man he is underneath the ledger and the pole. The line still waits in the rain. Doss still has to decide what to do with four strangers who suddenly know him better than his own captain does.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Whatever you're looking for, Sergeant—whoever you're afraid of losing—it's not in this line. These people just need to cross.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps out of the rain-shadows at the edge of the queue and approaches Sergeant Doss with the quiet certainty of someone who's read a situation correctly. She's not commanding or challenging him—she's just offering what she's seen in her silent watching. She speaks low, for his ears only, and her voice carries the weight of someone who's heard this kind of fear before, from crew members working night-barges, from people trying to survive.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: You know what you should do here, Sergeant. Do it, or step aside and let me through.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps closer to Doss, close enough that only the sergeant hears him. His voice drops to something hard and certain—not a threat, but a statement of fact. He's already read what's underneath the ledger and the pole; now he's just giving Doss the chance to choose which version of himself he wants to be. The refugees behind him are waiting in the rain, and Aldous will not turn back.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Sergeant, I can see what's weighing on you—and I think we might be able to help. But you need to tell us what you're actually afraid of.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen approaches Doss slowly and deliberately, keeping her hands visible and open. She lowers her voice so only he and the others nearby can hear, and studies his face with the quiet understanding of someone who has counseled many frightened people.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Sergeant, I know that weight. Tell me what you're hunting, and I'll help you find it—these refugees aren't your answer.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps closer to Doss, matching his posture and gaze like a soldier recognizing another. She stands without supplication or threat, just steady and present, her bearing unchanged from her years wearing a badge. She doesn't reach for his pole or loom over the queue—she simply waits, one guard to another, showing him she understands the burden he's carrying without asking him to compromise it.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Empathy: dice 0 0 0 + → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Doss's shoulders drop like a rope finally cut. He doesn't answer Mire's offer with words at first — he just looks past all four of them, out at the black water beyond the torchlight, the way a man looks at a grave he visits too often. "My girl went upriver to the temple two months back," he finally says, low enough that the queue can't hear. "Said she heard singing. I check every throat, every palm, telling myself I'll know her if she comes through hive-touched, and I won't have to be the one who — " He doesn't finish it. He doesn't have to. He steps back from the gate, waves the hooked pole toward the dark beyond it, and calls out to his men to "let the line move, we're behind schedule." The refugees surge forward, grateful and uncomprehending. As Ysolde, Aldous, Morwen and Mire pass through, Doss catches Aldous's sleeve just once. "If you hear that song out there," he says, "and you find a girl who still knows her own name — bring her back. I don't care what she's carrying." Then he turns back to his ledger, and the four of them walk on into Hollowmoot — stilt-town lanterns smeared gold through the downpour, the watchtower bell silent above the crowded market lanes.

ambiguities.issue: Arm A lists 'Attention', which the spec never defines.
ambiguities.detail: Arm definition lists Attention; not modelled.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Fate Core: boxes 1 and 2; Physique/Will +1/+2 adds a 3 box, +3 or more adds 3 and 4.
ambiguities.detail: stress boxes built with Fate Core values

ambiguities.issue: Does a GLOBAL anchor give the GM a free invoke like a GM card?
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Yes, GLOBAL cards placed on the rail give the GM 1 free invoke that scene.

ambiguities.issue: Tension was reduced by 1 (event 24, 'resolved -1') on the grounds that something was 'resolved,' but the log shows no face-up THREAT/FACTION card being tracked or taken out in this scene (no clock_change entries, no rail_add of a THREAT/FACTION type), and no explicit marker that a player's REACH goal was filled. The only card-like entity involved, Warden Sergeant Doss, is only formalized as a story card (NPC, SN-01) *after* the scene ends (event 25), not as a face-up THREAT/FACTION during play. The table's four rows don't obviously cover 'talked an NPC checkpoint into letting the party through' when no THREAT/FACTION card was ever put in play.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the checkpoint NPC as a stand-in for a THREAT that was effectively neutralized through social resolution, applying the -1 'resolved a THREAT' row by analogy.

ambiguities.issue: Event 11's compel invokes tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens' on card AL-02 as a normal (non-deck-draw) compel. The log does not show whether AL-02 was among the 3 cards left live in Aldous's binder or was the 1 card randomly placed into the Session Deck at session build (§4 step 2), in which case it would not be live and could not be compelled per §3.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Assumed AL-02 remained in Aldous's binder (live) since only one of his four cards enters the deck and the GM/engine allowed the compel to proceed without a deck-draw event.

ambiguities.issue: The engine refused a Beat Frame deployment because the stated trigger ('the party enters a settlement') was 'not an unused fictional trigger.' The spec's trigger-writing rules (§7) require a checkable WHEN/THEN event but never state whether a trigger can be reused within a session or is consumed after one use/attempt.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the engine's refusal as authoritative: the trigger was considered already spent/invalid, so no Beat Frame drew cards for this scene; the table moved on without disputing it.

cost_checks.note: This was a standard (non-deck-draw) Fate compel on a live card tag, not a §4 Session Deck draw cost — the provided cost-check record correctly shows draw_id as blank. The compel text ('reaching for a slate to send word up the line to Verrick's watchtower...') directly used the invoked tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens' from card AL-02, satisfying the general compel requirement that the aspect drive the complication. No §3-table deck-draw cost (tie/major-cost/minor-cost) occurred anywhere in this scene, so no other cost_check entries apply.

friction.text: The engine's rejection of the 'party enters a settlement' Beat Frame trigger (as 'not an unused fictional trigger') surfaced friction between the GM's narrative framing and the strict, checkable-event trigger format required by §7 — the spec doesn't clarify whether triggers are single-use or reusable, forcing an ad hoc interim ruling.

Three separate success-with-style results in one scene (events 14, 16, 22) all triggered the §3 'peek top card instead of a boost' option, and all three peeks landed on the same card (MI-01), left on top each time. The reward felt repetitive/low-value since nothing new was revealed after the first peek — a possible tuning issue with stacking success-with-style outcomes in a single scene.

The -1 Tension adjustment at scene end (event 24) lacked a clearly logged trigger condition (no THREAT/FACTION card was ever placed face-up or tracked with a clock in this scene), making it hard to audit against the §6 table without inferring intent.
